rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing in lecture bodies.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 3 (body, above the `<!-- maintainer -->` fence at L93): '*Referenced from: Module 5 (learn from the test, re-send packaged).*' — a module number + full module title inside shared body content, exactly the class of hit the rule's own pre-ship grep targets ('M[0-9] + module-name refs → each hit moves to the module file or dies'); the file's subject is Clean-Code-as-steering, not the arc, so the arc-lecture carve-out doesn't apply. The trace independently confirms the reader-facing cost: phase 1 confusion_flags[1] — 'Read cold ..., it reads as a citation to something the reader hasn't seen yet rather than a placement note — a half-beat of "wait, am I in the middle of something?" before the essay's own opening line resolves it.' This is not an isolated slip: `how-the-best-do-ci-cd.md` opens with the same shape ('*Supplementary for AE101 Module 6. Read after you've shipped your second skill.*'), while the other three AE101 supplementaries checked (`verification-asymmetry.md`, `backpressure.md`, `token-efficiency.md`) open directly on their H1/H2 with no module-naming byline at all — 2 of 5 checked carry the pattern, 3 don't, so this reads as an inconsistent convention rather than a deliberate universal one. Minor and self-resolving per the trace (not in its top-level ambiguous_instructions list), so non-blocking, but a real hit on the rule.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Drop the line-3 byline (the essay's own opening line resolves cold fine per the trace) and let the two linking module files carry the placement note, which they already do with richer context ('Optional prep in the Module 4 to Module 5 gap'). Since `how-the-best-do-ci-cd.md` carries the same pattern, this reads as a maintainer sweep decision across both files rather than a one-off fix on this file alone.
